course: an illustrated online course on academic philosophy for adults who never studied it
intro: The trunk runs in time order from Socrates to the present, one question a lesson. Each lesson opens on a real scene with real people, places and dates, asks the reader for a verdict before the argument, gives the argument and its strongest objection, and often ends on where the ideas stand among philosophers today. Plain, direct prose in the manner of Russell's History of Western Philosophy and Warburton's A Little History of Philosophy: opinions stated plainly, humour only from real facts, no aphorisms, no literary flourishes, no rhetorical questions. Legends are told as legends. Quotations come from named translations; do not change the words inside quotation marks.
